newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-SAfrica banks up profits, FNB lags.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-SAfrica banks up profits, FNB lags.

text.p: South Africa's First National Bank Holdings Ltd is set to post flat half year earnings, trailing robust growth at fellow banks Nedcor Ltd and Amalgamated Banks of South Africa Ltd.
The banks, three of the country's biggest, are set to post results over the next three weeks, kicking off with FNB -- subject of persistent takeover speculation -- next Wednesday.

Analysts said in spite of expected strong showings from some banks, the industry was still plagued by a margins' squeeze and hefty bad debts as it remained trapped in an environment of high operational costs and interest rates.
"The tight economic conditions are still a negative," said Mark Young, director of banking at international rating agency IBCA South Africa.
FNB was seen bearing the brunt of this, with Nedcor remaining resilient, able to increase market share, and Absa bouncing from a low earnings base a year ago.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast FNB's earnings for the six months ended March 31 rising to between 109.0 and 115.9 cents a share with consensus at 112.0 cents -- a slim increase of eight percent, the same as at its 1996 year end.
They expected a dividend of between 21.8 and 23.0 cents with consensus at 22.3 from 20.0 a year ago.

"Even though FNB has now sold off the McCarthy unit, they will still have for the period the bad debt provisions, and there's the rising expense in Wesbank," said Dave Southey, an analyst at Edey Rogers.
Weighed by heavy bad debts, FNB last December sold its troubled FirstPref instalment financing unit back to McCarthy Retail Ltd.
Another dampener to FNB earnings was that results were coming off a high base, analysts said.
By comparison Nedcor, which reports results for the six months to end-March on May 15, was seen sporting lending growth at a strong 20 percent on an annualised basis and sitting cash flush.
Although high bad debts were seen continuing, this would be offset by good performances from select operations, in particular the investment and merchant banking arms, analysts said.
"They will get a nice bounce from Syfrets again, and there has been a nice turnaround at UAL," Southey said.

Analysts expect Nedcor half year earnings in a range of 256.2 to 264.6 cents with consensus at 261.3 from 210.0 before -- a rise of 24.4 percent. They put the dividend at between 54 and 56.7 cents, averaging out at 55.4 cents from 45.0 last year.
Absa, which is due to release earnings for the year to end March on May 26, was seen showing profit growth of over 26 percent in spite of continued major technology costs and shrinking market share.
"The interesting one will be whether Absa will continue its upward growth off a low base. It has been losing market share across-the-board," IBCA's Young said.
Another analyst said Absa's lending growth rate had slowed to around 11 percent and its mortgage lending was growing near 12.6 percent, well below average industry expansion of 17 percent.
"It's going to put pressure on earnings growth next year," an analyst said.
However, a strong inflow of non-margin income was seen still boosting the bottom line this year.

Analysts forecast year earnings in a 223 to 228.8 cents band with consensus at 225.5 -- a gain of 26.7 percent from 178.0 in 1996. The dividend was seen between 70.8 and 75.5 cents with general expectations at 73.1 from 59 before.
Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd, the country's other main bank, will only report interim results in the second half of the year.
-- Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
